All-New Hyundai Elantra Wagon N Shines Darkly Across Imagination Land in Black With Red Accents
9 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show has few but important novelties – the 907-hp Lamborghini Temerario Spyder with a very cool vertical-folding hardtop, plus the launch of the all-new Hyundai Elantra and Rivian R2 along with some additional goodies from the likes of Acura or Honda.
Nothing big and nothing fancy, as if the Automobility LA and LA Auto Show (which are concurrent events) feared competing with the James Bond announcement from Amazon and the massive launch of Rockstar Games’ new Grand Theft Auto VI installment. Anyway, Hyundai is one of the major players at the ongoing show in California, which runs through November 29.
Aside from the all-new Hyundai Tucson, which celebrates its official North American public premiere in Los Angeles, the other massive novelty is the global introduction of the eighth-generation Elantra compact sedan. Known as the Avante at home in South Korea and launched in June 2026 at the Busan International Mobility Show, the model is an important bastion for affordable passenger cars in America.
That’s why Hyundai kept the launch of the all-new Elantra for Los Angeles instead of bringing it to Europe at the 2026 Paris Motor Show first. Anyway, the new model is larger, more angular, and also comes with a completely revamped interior featuring Hyundai's Pleos Connect infotainment system, plus revised ICE and hybrid powertrains.
Naturally, the launch of the all-new Hyundai Elantra has attracted a lot of attention – including across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI where a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has a fresh proposition for something cool: Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on a Hyundai station wagon for the Elantra nameplate.
We remember that the real compact car did have a touring option during the second generation’s stint in the late 1990s, followed by a five-door liftback for the third iteration. The fifth Elantra was also offered as a two-door coupe, but just recently the pixel master wanted to see it go up against the flurry of crossover SUVs with a practical body style.
More precisely, the CGI expert envisioned the all-new Hyundai Elantra as a high-riding Cross Wagon akin to high-riding premium options like the new Audi A6 Allroad, making it a very direct alternative to compact crossover SUVs. It was dressed in a cool shade of Sage Green to show it off as both an adventurous and elegant option at the same time. But was that enough?
Nope, as it turns out! Now the author is back fiddling with the Hyundai Elantra station wagon, and this time around we’re dealing with the unofficial, hypothetical N design project, a high-performance station wagon with a sporty flair – after all, it’s dressed completely in black, even the alloy wheels, save for the classic Hyundai N red accents. What do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)

Home/ Office Entry
Mobile
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-LCD Screen 1
Sabrent sent us this charger, and while we do not generally review USB chargers, we thought we would take a few photos and share it since it has been pretty useful. The Voltik 252W 8-port USB PD 3.0 Charger is a desktop charging station with four USB-C ports and four USB-A ports, and Sabrent rates it at 252W of total output. That is a lot of power for something that sits on a desk, and the port layout is what makes it worth a closer look.
Here is the unit via an Amazon Affiliate link .
Sabrent Voltik 252W Hardware Overview
The enclosure is a black rectangular block that is not really what we would want from a travel charger, but it works well on a desk.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-Front Angled 1
The front face has a display at the top, then the four USB-C ports, then the four USB-A ports below them. There is also a button for the LCD.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-USB Type-C Ports 1
The USB-C ports are arranged in two rows of two. The upper row is labeled C1A and C1B, and the lower row is labeled C2A and C2B. Sabrent rates each USB-C port at up to 100W, which is enough for a laptop on its own. The 252W figure is the station’s combined output, so the four USB-C ports cannot all deliver 100W at the same time. Sabrent lists support for PD 3.0, PPS, QC 4.0, and QC 3.0.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-USB Type-A Ports 1
Below the USB-C ports are the four USB-A ports, also in two rows, with the Sabrent logo underneath. Sabrent rates each USB-A port at up to 18W.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-LCD Screen 1
Here is a shot of the LCD lit up and showing eight port boxes labeled C1A, C2A, A1A, and A2A across the top and C1B, C2B, A1B, and A2B across the bottom. The screen can cycle through each port to show current wattage, voltage, amperage, and internal temperature by using the button between ports C1A and C1B. Other chargers do that, but if you do not have something like that yet, then it is something that if you read STH, you will like.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-Bottom 1
The power-input panel has the AC inlet, a printed rating label that includes the model AX-8PTC and the per-port and shared output modes. It is nice that the unit directly takes AC power rather than through an external power brick.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-Power Cable 1
Of course, if you want to use it on the road, it is pretty easy to find a different input cable for this one.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-Rear 1
The rear face has two long raised strips along its edges and two rectangular recesses in the center for a mounting plate.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-Mount Kit 1
The mounting plate has four fixing holes and two rectangular hooks, shown here with two black fixings in front and the charger behind. That hardware points to mounting the station rather than leaving it loose on the desktop.
Final Words
The Sabrent Voltik 252W is interesting because it consolidates a desk full of chargers into one unit with eight ports and a display that shows the status of each port’s voltage, current, temperature, and time. It is quite useful to know if something is charging, or if it is on, and how fast. On the other hand, we have seen notebooks that draw over 100W via USB Type-C, so even though this is a huge USB charger, it cannot charge everything.
Sabrent 252W 8-Port USB Desktop Charging Station-Front 1
For a desk with several devices that need to charge, that combination of port count, power, and feedback is the practical case for a single station in place of a drawer full of separate adapters. We now have four of these.
Where to Buy
If you want to buy one of these or check the current pricing, here is an Amazon affiliate link .

EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Lamborghini Temerario Spyder: Is It the Go-To Open-Top Supercar of the Moment?
8 photos
Photo: Lamborghini
Imagine this: you just hit the jackpot or inherited a huge amount of money and you want an open-top supercar. Which model do you choose?
Well, there are quite a few models to choose from. Porsche’s 911 Turbo S Cabriolet is more of a daily driver. Ferrari’s 296 GTS is definitely on the list, and so are the Artura Spider and 750S Spider from McLaren. There is also a newcomer to the segment. It’s the Raging Bull’s new open-top “baby” supercar, which adds the Spyder suffix to the Temerario.
We knew it was coming even before Lamborghini pulled the wraps off the Temerario more than two years ago. That’s because its predecessors, including the Huracan and the Gallardo, were all offered in this configuration, in addition to the fixed-roof body styles, and over the years, the convertible variants came in all kinds of different configurations, some of which were more track-focused than others.
Therefore, it was not exactly a surprise when we saw the first prototypes of the new open-top Lambo earlier this year doing their thing in the open, with their bodies fully wrapped in camouflage to the point where it was almost impossible to catch a decent glimpse at the thing that separates it from the regular model. That would be the folding hardtop, which represents a major step up from the rag top of its predecessors.
This is the company’s first-ever retractable hardtop supercar, and while some might argue that a folding fabric roof would have lowered the center of gravity, while also keeping the weight in check, others would say that this is the best possible choice for such a thing. By the way, let’s not forget that models such as the Aventador Roadster and the Diablo VT roadster featured split panels, though they had to be manually removed and stowed.
Photo: Lamborghini When it comes to the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder, the roof lowers and raises at the push of a button. This component features ten electric actuators and not an electro-hydraulic system, which would have been the more traditional approach. And it is definitely worth noting that the Artura Spider and the 296 GTS from McLaren and Ferrari, respectively, also benefit from hardtops.
Lamborghini’s new Temerario Spyder has a dry weight of 3,979 pounds (1,805 kg), and that makes it exactly 220 pounds (100 kg) heavier than its fixed roof sibling, which tips the scale at 3,759 lbs (1,705 kg( dry. The front-to-rear weight distribution has changed from 43.4% front - 56.6% rear to 43.2% front - 56.8% rear, the spec sheet reveals. As for the total length, width, and height, these remain the same, and so does the space between the axles.
Another thing that hasn’t changed is the plug-in hybrid powertrain. The 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine, which can be revved all the way up to 10,000 rpm, still develops 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) between 9,000 and 9,750 rpm. The V8 is assisted by three axial-flux electric motors, and the total system output is 907 hp (920 ps/677 kW). From 0 to 62 mph (0-100 kph), the Temerario Spyder needs 2.8 seconds, which is 0.1 seconds slower than the Temerario Coupe, and at 213 mph (343 kph), the top speed is the same.
A carry-over aluminum spaceframe chassis, carbon ceramic brakes, a retuned suspension compared to its fixed-roof sibling , an eight-speed automatic transmission, all-wheel drive, an aluminum body, 9x20-inch wheels at the front and 11.5x21-inch wheels at the rear, and others are thing, including the front and rear damping system (Lamborghini MagneRide), and the front and rear double wishbone suspension.
Photo: Lamborghini The Lamborghini Temerario Spyder also benefits from a three-level neck warmer in order to keep the occupants warm in cold temperatures. There is also a power-operated rear window that allows the cockpit to be bathed in the exhaust sound when it is lowered, even with the roof raised. The Raging Bull says that the model can accommodate individuals up to 6 feet and 7 inches (2 meters) tall, and that makes it more spacious than the demised Huracan Evo Spyder.
In addition to the open-top design, complete with the special compartment behind the seats, the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder sets itself apart from the Temerario Coupe by featuring hexagonal cowls behind the headrests. Interested parties can choose from a plethora of paint finishes for the exterior and interior colors, and those numbers further increase if you bring Ad Personam, which is Lambo’s personalization division, into discussion.
Before wrapping things up, we have to remind you that the Temerario Spyder is not the first open-top Lambo from the company’s new-age lineup, because that model would be the rare Fenomeno Roadster . However, the latter does not feature a retractable hardtop, a soft top, a targa design, nor a removable panel, as it is permanently open. Production is capped at 15 units in this case, whereas its fixed-roof variant is limited to 29 examples. And this makes the Fenomeno a “few-off” supercar.
It is only a matter of time until Lamborghini introduces the Revuelto Roadster, and it will be interesting to see what path it will choose for the roof. Still, if we had to guess, we’d say that probably a manually-removable one.
Meanwhile, if you had deep pockets (or maybe you do), and wanted to spruce up your weekend (or perhaps daily) drives with a modern-day convertible supercar, would you pick the new Lamborghini Temerario Spyder ? I know I would, but then again, I’ve always been a Lambo fan!

439-Mile Survivor 1969 Hemi GTX Ragtop Breaks Cover at MCACN After 36 Years on Jackstands
26 photos
Photo: Facebook/Robert Carl
How is it possible that certain Hemi Mopars reach 2026 with fewer than 500 original miles on the clock, most of them accumulated in 1,320-foot increments? Here is one such unicorn, Mr. Motech’s 1969 Plymouth GTX “GTXterminator” ragtop race car. It just broke cover at the Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals, after a long 36-year spent on jack stands.
During the height of Detroit's horsepower wars, select 426-cubic-inch machines skipped daily street duty entirely. Purchased solely to conquer quarter-mile drag strips, they traveled from garage to racetrack on open trailers before slipping into quiet hibernation, preserving factory sheet metal and astonishingly low odometer readings across nearly 60 years.
One of the rarest examples of that phenomenon commanded attention during its unveiling at the 2026 Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals, documented by Geoff Stunkard on his YouTube channel, Geoff Stunkard's Zookeeper's Diary. This bright metallic blue 1969 Plymouth Hemi GTX convertible displays just 439 documented original miles. Originally owned and campaigned by John Tedder, it stands as one of only 11 U.S.-market 1969 Hemi GTX convertibles ever produced.
Tedder was far from an ordinary weekend racer; a prominent Chrysler insider known as "Mr. MoTech," he founded the MoTech program and once resolved a Maryland titling snag caused by bumperless Plymouth Superbirds. Ordered under the Tedder & Ulrich banner specifically to battle Chevrolets in NHRA Super Stock E Automatic and SS/FA competition, the GTX scored a class-winning ET of 11.86 seconds at 117.84 mph, recorded at the 1969 Winternationals.
Photo: Facebook/Robert Carl That was only the beginning; during a blistering 1970 campaign, Tedder's Hemi ragtop reigned as the top SS/EA contender in the nation, sweeping class victories at the 1970 Winternationals, the 1970 Gatornationals, and the 1970 Springnationals while also capturing Super Stock Eliminator Runner-Up honors at the Gatornationals.
Back then, the convertible cut an unmistakable profile at the starting line, painted blue across its nose and white along its tail, topped by a convertible roof painted black forward and white behind. Once its competitive career concluded, the Plymouth's survival became a saga of fortunate timing.
In 1983, a prospective buyer placed a $500 deposit and never returned, even though Tedder had already mailed the title. About a year later in the mid-1980s, Tedder phoned an enthusiast named Don, who had bought an identically configured 1969 440-cubic-inch 4-speed GTX convertible new. Don hooked an open trailer to a Dodge Dakota and hauled the 182-mile Hemi Mopar home.
Photo: Facebook/William Pearce An Air Force serviceman stationed in Shreveport, Louisiana, first encountered the convertible at a 1987 local Mopar club gathering, committing its details to memory. By 1990, Don placed the Plymouth onto jack stands, beginning an unbroken 36-year slumber.
Around 2014, while preparing to move back to Maryland, Tedder spotted the car's original 426-cubic-inch block—which had spun its number-one bearing decades earlier—resting beneath his workbench, phoned Don, and reunited the matching-numbers engine with its chassis.
Nearly 40 years after that Shreveport meeting, the former airman answered a Moparts wanted ad for space-saver wheels, recognized the Louisiana area code, and asked about Don. That chance conversation connected current owner Robert Carl and his mechanic to Don's family. Following a year of respectful negotiations, the family entrusted the GTX to Carl as its next caretaker, finally lowering the historic drag car off jack stands for the first time since 1990.
Photo: Facebook/Robert Carl Wisely resisting a full restoration, the new owner preserved the 439-mile survivor with all original sheet metal, its original fender tag, and its complete numbers-matching drivetrain intact under metallic blue paint and blue vinyl upholstery.
Awakening it required pulling the distributor, priming the oiling system, flushing stale fuel and fluids, adjusting the valvetrain, and replacing brittle convertible-top hydraulic lines. It’s probably one of the car’s rare top-down public appearances, since Tedder raced it roof-up.
That extraordinary survivor belongs to one of Detroit's most distinctive muscle car lineages. Debuting for 1967 as the upscale Belvedere GTX before standing alone from 1968 through 1971 , Plymouth's B-body flagship earned billing as the "gentleman's muscle car."
Photo: Facebook/Robert Carl Unlike stripped-down street brawlers, it paired bucket-seat comfort and heavy-duty suspension with a standard 440-cubic-inch, 375-horsepower Super Commando V8, leaving the 426-cube, 425-horsepower Street Hemi as its ultimate option before reverting to a Road Runner package through 1974.
Higher showroom pricing and internal competition from the wildly popular Road Runner kept GTX sales modest throughout its standalone run. Mother Mopar built 12,690 units in 1967, peaked at 18,940 in 1968, eased to 15,602 in 1969, tumbled to 7,748 in 1970, and closed at 2,942 in 1971. All in all, just 57,922 cars were sold.
GTX convertibles lasted just 3 years: 680 in 1967, 1,026 in 1968, and 700 in 1969. Specify the legendary Street Hemi, and those production figures shrink dramatically. Across all five standalone model years from 1967 through 1971, Plymouth produced just 1,490 Hemi GTXs combined.
Photo: Facebook/Robert Carl Yearly output declined steadily as insurance surcharges climbed and emissions rules tightened: 733 examples in 1967, 446 in 1968, 209 in 1969, 72 in 1970, and only 30 in 1971, closing the curtain on Chrysler's iconic 426-cubic-inch V8.
Breaking down 1969 production underscores how scarce Tedder's machine truly is. Of 15,602 GTXs assembled, 14,902 were two-door hardtops; 700 were convertibles, and comprised 689 440 models, plus 11 Hemis: four 4-speeds and seven automatics. This is one of those magnificent seven Torqueflite examples (the automatic was the preferred solution by drag racers).
In 1969, ordering a Hemi GTX convertible demanded real money. The convertible opened at $3,635—$219 above the $3,416 hardtop—and adding the 426 Hemi cost $656, lifting its base sticker to $4,291 before mandatory heavy-duty equipment.
Over the past five years, Hemi GTX convertibles sales yield a $166,375 median, while the record (for both a 1969 model and any Hemi GTX convertible) remains a $230,000 from a Mecum auction in 2017 ($253k with buyer’s fee). I wonder what this unicorn would go for, if it were for sale.

Dealer Selling 2020 Ford GT With 3,000 Miles and You're Very Lucky if You Can Afford It
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
It’s been four years since the Ford GT story ended, and so far, the Blue Oval hasn’t announced anything about a possible successor to its iconic supercar.
The last example of the second generation rolled off the line north of the US border, at Markham, Ontario, Canada, in late 2022, thus marking the end of an era. And while there is no successor anywhere in sight, those who want a blue-blooded GT from the Dearborn-based automaker in their garage have nothing else to do than search the used car market for that example that looks perfect to them.
Does the one pictured in the gallery tick this box? Well, in that case, you are in luck, because it is indeed searching for a new home on the used car market in the States. This Ford GT features a yellow paint finish on the outside, has racing strips in black with a gray center stretching across its length, from the front bumper to the rear hood and wing, and benefits from other black details on the lower parts of the body and not only.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago The wheels may appear black too, but upon closer inspection, you will see that they have been made of carbon fiber, and actually feature a dry look. The EcoBoost engine is visible at the rear even without popping the hood open, courtesy of the transparent cover. And it is a twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6, in case you forgot, it initially pumped out 647 horsepower (483 kW/656 ps).
From the 2020 model year onward , the engine was tuned to produce 660 horsepower (492 kW669 ps). With no modifications whatsoever, the second-generation Ford GT brags about running the standing quarter mile in 10.6 seconds. The 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) sprint is a 2.9-second affair, and the top speed stands at 216 mph (348 kph). Not too shabby.
A look inside the pictured Ford GT reveals that the cockpit has been dressed in black Alcantara. You can see the upholstery on the seats, steering wheel, lower and upper parts of the dashboard panel, and other components. Carbon fiber trim is also on deck, and so is white stitching for some contrast.
As mentioned in the title, this American supercar is a 2020 model year, and at the time of cataloging, it had around 3,000 miles (~4,800 km) or so on the odometer. That’s what the vendor, @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram, claims. The dealer accepts trades, offers financing, and asks for $1,099,995 for the Ford GT in question, and that’s why we said that you are very lucky if you can afford this thing.
But if you had all the money in the world, would you pay $1.1 million for this low-mileage example? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)

Third-Gen Fiat Strada X Adopts the Grande Panda Styling But Remains Extremely Practical Even in CGI
7 photos
Photo: kdesignag / Instagram
America has a special relation with pickup trucks; there is no doubt about it. Alas, there are particularities with this affair. North America loves the humongous beasts like the Ford Super Duty and the Ram 1500 TRX SRT or the Toyota Tacoma. South America, meanwhile, likes them smaller and nimbler.
Latin America has a culture for pickup trucks just like North America, but over there it’s not all about who has the biggest towed trailer or the most prestigious trim level. It’s also about everyday passenger car-like agility blended with real utility, and at a price that doesn’t require selling a villa or an arm and a leg.
That’s why models like the Fiat Strada , Ram 700, Volkswagen Saveiro, Chevrolet Montana, Fiat Toro, Ram Rampage, or the Renault Oroch thrive across the continent, offering good fuel economy, rugged styling without bulkiness, and massive variety plus a great work-to-weekend ratio. It’s no wonder that Volkswagen, for example, is striving to expand its offerings with the all-new Tukan, or Fiat is offering both the Strada and Toro.
Actually, the Fiat Strada coupe utility is also known as the Ram 700 in markets like Mexico. It’s been around since 1998 across two generations, with the current one launched in production in Brazil in 2020. It has already gone through an encompassing mid-cycle refresh procedure for the 2024 model year, so everyone – including the rumor mill – expects the Italians to come up with a brand-new generation sometime around the 2028 model year to make sure it remains competitive.
Naturally, that also attracted the attention of the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators, and one of them decided to stop dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to envision the upcoming third-generation Fiat Strada in their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project.
More precisely, Kleber Silva, a Brazil-based virtual artist known as " KDesign AG " on social media, has decided to have a CGI go at imagining the next-gen coupe utility and dubbed it Fiat Strada X to stand out in any wishful-thinking crowd. According to the pixel master, the next iteration could be inspired by the funky and recent Fiat Grande Panda supermini, which is based on the Stellantis Smart Car platform shared with the likes of the Fiat Grizzly, Citroen C3, and the latest Opel Frontera.
It could easily adopt both the architecture and the pixel-style exterior design, and the CGI expert even went as far as to create two distinct versions – the double-cab Ranch model featuring a T200 MHEV powertrain (1.0-liter 3-cylinder turbo with 12V BSG packing up to 130 hp) and the work-focused Endurance single-cab model. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by KDesign AG - (@kdesignag)

Audi’s New RS 5 Coupe Wants a Piece of the BMW M4 – Rendering
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik
Unless you’ve been living under a rock these past couple of years, then you know that the third generation A5 is not exactly an A5, but an A4. Or, better said, the B9’s successor.
The reason is simple, as the four-ring brand wanted to use odd numbers on its ICE-powered cars and even numbers for EVs, though this decision was eventually dropped, as it would have been too confusing for the company’s clients. However, before it did that, the new A5 was already out, and rumor has it that its mid-cycle refresh, which could be a couple of years away, might bring back the A4 moniker.
Audi’s all-new A5 (B10) is offered in two body styles. The sedan is not exactly a sedan, but a five-door liftback, and the Avant is a five-door station wagon. They both come to life at the same factory in Germany, namely Neckarsulm, and if you live in China, then you actually get a four-door version of the model, which is called the A5 L Sedan. The “L” in its name stands for “long wheelbase,” and it is joined by a stretched version of the A5 Sportback.
Regardless of the body style and configuration, all version of the model are based on the same Premium Platform Combustion (PPC) architecture. The construction is also the foundation stone of the new-gen Q5, which remains a high-riding alternative to the A5, as well as the bigger A6. The latter is the new generation, which goes up against the likes of the Mercedes E-Class and BMW 5 Series. The new-gen Q7 is also based on this construction, and so is the first-ever Q9, aka the brand’s full-size SUV.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Audi’s new-gen A5 is also marketed in the United States, with an MSRP of $50,400 for the 2027 model year, which has 268 hp (272 ps/200 kW) and 295 lb-ft (400 Nm) of torque from a 2-liter four-pot, taking 5.6 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from zero. A 7-speed S tronic automatic transmission channels everything to the standard quattro all-wheel drive system.
The S5 is next in line, priced from $63,600. It too features a seven-speed automatic transmission and standard quattro all-wheel drive, and has 362 horsepower (367 ps/270 kW) and 406 pound-feet (550 Nm) of torque on tap. The 3.0-liter V6 TFSI engine enables this model to hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 4.3 seconds, or 1.3 seconds faster than the regular A5.
A brand new Audi RS 5 is also out, though it will arrive in the United States of America sometime in 2027, with pricing to be announced. Still, it will sit at the top of the family, and in case you forgot, it has 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW) and 443 lb-ft (600 Nm) of torque produced by its 2.0-liter twin-turbo V6. An electric motor assists it, generating 174 hp (177 ps/130 kW) and 339 lb-ft (460 Nm) of torque.
The total output is 630 hp (639 ps/470 kW) and the assembly produces 608 pound-feet (825 Nm) of torque combined. From 0 to 60 mph (97 kph), it takes roughly three and a half seconds. Quattro all-wheel drive, dynamic torque vectoring, and an electromechanical torque vectoring transaxle are also on deck, and the model can travel for around 50 miles (80 km) on electric power.
Photo: Instagram | Kelsonik Audi’s new-gen RS 5 is offered as an RS 5 Sedan and RS 5 Avant , and chances are the latter will be kept away from the USA, as only the former is expect to make its way over here. At the same time, the automaker does not intend to offer a two-door version of this model, and that means that it does not have a rival to the likes of the BMW M4, nor the upcoming Mercedes-AMG CLE 63.
Is that a good decision? Only time will tell if the answer is yes or no, and while such a thing may not exist in the real world, it does in Fantasy Land, where @kelsonik recently sketched it out, sharing it on social media. This rendered 2027 Audi RS 5 Coupe has the same design overall as the rest of the lineup, albeit instead of five doors, it has only two. It looks a lot sportier, and for what it’s worth, something like this would definitely take a proper swing at the BMW M4 Coupe.
Now, assuming Audi had an RS 5 Coupe in its lineup and you were shopping for a cool two-door premium sports model with a fixed-roof design, would you get this one, or the M4? Or would you perhaps wait for the first-ever Mercedes- AMG CLE 63 to finally break cover? The latter is a very interesting proposal, as it will feature a V8 engine, presumably with a little over 600 horsepower available via the right pedal, and what should be a great soundtrack in the track-ready drive mode. Ferrari SP Modulo and Spider Come From Behind the CGI Curtain as Fantasy Land's New Special Projects
9 photos
Photo: uygarspots / Instagram
This week, unlike others, has been pretty busy for a November month that’s usually damp and dreary. But the automotive world never sleeps, as it turns out. And if it’s not directly overboard, connecting elements will ensure its flow, nevertheless.
So, we just kicked off the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show in California, an event that runs through November 29, and the novelties were few but extremely important, like the gorgeous and finally not-boring-anymore 907-hp Lamborghini Temerario Spyder, which has a vertical-hiding hardtop roof mechanism that lowers its center of gravity.
There was also the Rivian R2 and the all-new eighth generation of the compact and affordable Hyundai Elantra, among others. But the miscellaneous things were pretty bonkers, too: the entire planet felt like it stood still while consoles loaded the new Grand Theft Auto VI after 13 years of waiting, and Amazon dropped the James Bond bombshell in the person of Robert Pattinson turning up as the new 007.
With all the commotion, one would be excused if anyone decided to time out and zone out for a while. Nope, not the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to bring us new unofficial, hypothetical design projects even during these event-rich times.
For example, Uygar, a "professional daydreamer" based in Turkey and known as ' uygarspots ' on social media, has apparently decided that a brand-new Ferrari, or two, could also join the party of novelties – even if only from across Imagination Land. So, he cooked up a new Ferrari SP idea.
The Ferrari SP traditionally stands for things like a Sport Prototipo or a Special Project, and there have been early 1960s Prancing Horses wearing the moniker. In recent times, it has been used for both unique projects as well as the limited-series Icona models - Monza SP1 and Monza SP2 or the Daytona SP3.
Now the pixel master has decided to combine the modern Ferrari SP vision with a name used for a one-off 1970 concept sports car designed by Paolo Martin at Pininfarina based on the Ferrari 512 S – the famous Modulo prototype.
His idea, as far as we can tell, is a personal project, and doesn’t involve using the extreme look of the Pininfarina Modulo prototype, just the name. Instead, it is now a more traditional two-door sports car with a mid-engine arrangement and flowing aerodynamic elements, plus gullwing doors on the coupe variant. No worries, it’s not a Luce, as there are massive dual exhaust outlets around the back, tucked left and right between the wide LED rear lights and the humongous diffuser.
But wait, there is more. If you like the idea, which uses Ferrari’s current design language – for example, the front black visor element- there’s a second option if you don’t want to play with gullwing doors. The CGI expert has also cooked up a Spider version!
This one instead has Lambo-style doors and absolutely no roof in sight - something that is easy to achieve in Fantasy Land but harder to live with in the real world. However, it's still pretty darn cool, right? Would you like Ferrari to create something like this? How About a New 1,200-HP Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 To Quench Your Muscle Car Thirst?
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | jesus.spec
You may be tempted to think that there are a few typos in the title. After all, 1,200 horsepower does not sound like the standard output when it comes to this model, and where would you find a new one given that production of the S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 concluded a few years ago?
Well, on the used car market, of course, especially if you know where to look and are patient enough. We recently stumbled upon quite a few such muscle cars that caught our attention, and the one pictured above sits at the very top of the list. That’s because it indeed features a lot more power than the original Bugatti Veyron, and it has a renowned tuner based in the Lone Star State to thank for that.
We are talking about none other than Hennessey, which gave it a jaw-dropping amount of power. The output is not actually rated at 1,200 hp, because this machine actually has 1,204 hp (1,221 ps/898 kW ) courtesy of the Venom 1200 package , and the massively upgraded 5.2-liter supercharged V8 engine now pumps out 902 pound-feet (1,223 Nm) of torque. However, you will need to put E85 in the fuel tank in order to obtain these numbers.
With no mods whatsoever, the S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 has 760 hp (771 ps/567 kW) and 627 lb-ft (847 Nm) of torque to play with. It hits 60 mph (97 kph) in a little over three seconds, and needs 10.7 seconds officially to complete the standing quarter mile.
Photo: Instagram | jesus.spec Only 66 units of the Venom 1200-equipped Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 saw the light of day, featuring a few other extras besides the neck-snapping power boost, and pictured above is one of them. With 937 miles (1,508 km) on the odometer, this 2022 model year machine is pretty much brand new, so if you wanted to spruce up your weekends, or perhaps daily drives, with something like this, then you have come to the right place.
That’s because this ride is indeed searching for a new home in the United States of America, and besides the aftermarket goodies, it also sports the Carbon Fiber Track Package, the listing reveals. It is finished in white, has several glossy black details, the Hennessey name on the windscreen, the Venom 1200 decals on the side skirt, tinted windows, and other special touches all around. The interior mixes black and white Alcantara and leather upholstery, and looks very good from what we can tell.
How much do you think this Hennessey-tuned Venom 1200 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 costs? Well, it’s not cheap, that’s for sure, but it’s ridiculously expensive either. At the time of writing, this muscle car had a sticker price of $144,995 attached to it. It’s advertised on social media by @jesus.spec, and the selling dealer says that nationwide shipping is available, albeit likely at an extra cost. So, have you found your next cool ride? The last time Hyundai announced a new work truck was 22 years ago, and the Hyundai Porter has proven itself as a dependable workhorse throughout Korea and Southeast Asia – but only the pyramids and the Chevy Express can last forever. Hyundai is reportedly getting ready to pull the wraps off an all-new Porter pickup. This time, it’s electric .
Distinct from the Piaggio-branded Porter pickup that’s already sold in Europe , the Hyundai Porter is a conceptually similar, work-focused vehicle with a dropside pickup “bed” trailing a box-like passenger cab and a serious, professional-grade payload capacity .
Carscoops recently published photos of a heavily camouflaged Hyundai Porter prototype last month, along with claims that Hyundai means to follow up the success of sister brand Kia’s multifunctional PV5 electric vans with a globally available electric version of the truck as early as next year. This week, the wraps came off , giving us our best look yet at what the truck might look like when it makes its official debut.
Something like this
Made with AI.
After feeding as many spy shots as I could into some AI models , we ended up with the images you see here. If they’re accurate, they show a commercial-ready EV that’s meant to attract new fleet buyers looking to ditch diesel in Western markets while serving as a direct, 1:1 replacement for domestic fleet operators already putting Porter pickups to work.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Those operators will probably feel a little safer behind the wheel of the new truck, too. Hyundai has worked a short hood and crash structure into the bodywork where a conventional “flat” cabover now sits – a move that seems to point both to a commitment to provide better front-end protection to the truck’s occupants and an intent to at least take an honest run at the Euro NCAP crash standards .
Beyond that, we don’t really know anything about the upcoming Korean pickup – but it’s a safe bet that the next-generation Porter will benefit from some of the technology that’s been baked into the Hyundai Motor Group’s E-GMP.S commercial vehicle platform that underpins the Kia PV vehicles. Those ship with 51.5 and 71.2 kWh battery options sending electrons to 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motors, and while that’s far from a guarantee, it’s not nothing , either.
That’s my take, anyway – what’s yours? Will the Hyundai Porter EV make its way to the West on an AWD version of the E-GMP.S platform, or will it remain a regional model running on one of the company’s hybrid platforms? Let us know in the comments.
